Ava: Noticing a canary stuck in REPORTING for private VPC cluster eu-west-2-pprod. Control plane shows config v12, agents still on v10. Anyone else seeing propagation lag?
Sam: Yup — saw it ~10m ago. Agents on that fleet are pulling but backoff loops. CLI shows "agent-sync: backoff 30s" on several nodes.
Priya: Are these air-gapped? We pushed fw rule changes last night, could be related.
deploy-bot: canary-deploy-2026-03-23-1142 started: canary_id=cd-9832, target=eu-west-2-pprod, intended_split=5%
Neil: Quick thought — we rely on control-plane guards for canary cutovers today. For private/VPC where propagation can be delayed, we should enforce a secondary guard in the agent so rollout doesn't assume central sync.
Ava: Agreed. Right now the console shows cluster-level status only; ops can't tell which agents applied the canary. Need per-agent visibility.
Sam: Adding per-node metrics sounds right: agent.config_version, agent.last_sync_ts, agent.sync_backoff_count. That would make dashboards actionable.
Priya: For air-gapped installs we absolutely can't assume real-time CP->agent. Agents need an offline policy with local rollback triggers (error-rate, latency spike, oom).
Neil: Example agent-side policy I sketched:
```yaml
rollout:
  mode: canary
  traffic_split: 0.05
  guard:
    monitor_window: 60s
    error_rate_threshold: 0.05
    local_rollback: true
```
The agent will sample traffic deterministically and monitor local metrics; if thresholds breach it flips traffic to baseline and emits an event.
Ava: How do we ensure distributed splits remain close to intended when agents are on mixed versions? If some agents still on v10 and others v12 we could skew buckets.
Neil: Use deterministic hashing at the agent ingress (hash(user_id) < weight) with a per-config seed derived from config_version. If agent sees a version mismatch it serves baseline until sync completes. That avoids half-applied canaries.
Sam: But that could temporarily reduce effective canary traffic if many agents delay. Console should show "effective split" vs "intended split".
Priya: UX request: show per-cluster "enforced_locally" flag and a warning when CP and agent config_version differ by >1. Also surface which agents are in fallback mode.
Ava: On quotas/gates: should split enforcement be at gateway (ingress) or agent? For private tenants there can be multiple gateways per cluster.
Neil: Storing the sampling policy in the agent avoids central coordination. Gateway can be thin proxy. Advantage: offline-safe. Disadvantage: depends on agent rollout.
Sam: Short-term mitigation: add a deploy-bot command to force-publish to a specific cluster with approval: `rctl publish --target eu-west-2-pprod --force` — that bypasses queue but we need SRE sign-off.
Priya: For air-gapped customers, also support a disk-backed `canary-policy.json` that the agent will read if it can't reach CP for X minutes. That makes local rollbacks deterministic.
Ava: Ok, I'll draft an RFC with options: control-plane-only, agent-side-only, hybrid (CP for intent + agent enforcement), telemetry additions, and UI changes (effective vs intended split, per-agent sync view). Want co-authors: @Neil @Priya?
Priya: +1, I can write the private/VPC constraints and air-gap section.
Neil: I'll add the deterministic sampling design and failure modes.
Sam: I'll scope the telemetry + dashboard changes and a small migration plan.
Ava: Also add a quick temporary alert: fire when cluster-config-drift > 1 for >5m (so SREs can triage before rollouts).
deploy-bot: Note: fw rule change #3425 was applied 2026-03-23 09:12 UTC.
Ava: Thanks — putting the RFC in #eng-platform drafts today. :thumbsup:
